subject: Performance SLOs & customer-led load test plan
messages:
From: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@finwise.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@finwise.com>
Date: 2027-04-18T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: Performance SLOs & load test plan

Hi Logan,

Thanks again for the call this morning — helpful discussion. Quick recap of the performance targets we discussed and next steps for the customer-led load test:

- Targets:
  - P95 latency: <= 250ms for full response (non-streaming paths)
  - Streaming: partial token latency <= 100ms for first chunk
  - Sustained throughput: 500 requests/sec
  - Concurrency: support up to 200 concurrent sessions

- Notes:
  - We will exercise both standard generation and streaming chat flows.
  - KV cache warm-up is acceptable; we'd like guidance on expected warm-up time and how it affects metrics.

- Load test plan (customer-led):
  - We'll run k6 scripts from our test infra (we can provide the scripts).
  - Requires a test API token and an allowlist of Redwood test IP ranges.
  - Preferred test windows: Apr 20 10:00-14:00 PT (primary) and Apr 21 09:00-12:00 PT (backup).

Can you confirm you can provision a short-lived test token, provide the endpoint and IP ranges to allowlist, and share any runbook or expected measurement points we should collect?

Thanks,

Sarah Kim
Director of EngOps
FinWise
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@finwise.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-18T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Performance SLOs & load test plan

Hi Sarah — great speaking with you as well. Thanks for the clear targets; below is a quick confirmation and an initial plan from our side.

Recap/answers:
- P95 <= 250ms for non-streaming paths: noted. We'll validate against P95 and P99 as part of the run.
- Streaming: we'll measure first-chunk latency; 100ms target noted.
- Throughput/concurrency: we'll aim to validate sustained 500 req/s with bursts to 750 req/s and concurrency up to 200.
- KV/cache warm-up: expect approx 5-10 minutes of warm-up for common prefixes depending on model and prompt size; we'll include a warm-up stage in the runbook.

What Redwood will provide:
- Dedicated test endpoint (staging) for FinWise: https://staging-api.redwood.example/finwise
- Short-lived API token: TEST-FINWISE-20270420 (will expire Apr 22)
- IP allowlist ranges to give to your infra team:
  - 34.80.12.5/32
  - 34.80.12.6/32
  - 34.80.12.7/32

Suggested test window (confirming yours): Apr 20 10:00-14:00 PT. We can also support Apr 21 backup. Please confirm timezone for your runners; we'll coordinate capacity on our side.

Runbook and measurements we'll collect (we'll also share these as a PDF):
- P50/P95/P99 latency for full response and for streaming first-chunk.
- Throughput curve (RPS vs latency) and error rates.
- Concurrency breakdown and tail latencies.
- Token consumption and cost estimate for the run.

If you can send the k6 scripts ahead of time (or link to a repo), our SREs will sanity-check and flag any changes required.

I'll loop in Marissa and Rishi to own the run coordination and infra prep.

Best,

Logan Wright
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-18T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Follow-up: Performance SLOs & load test plan

Forwarding Sarah's note and Logan's confirmation. Action items below — please treat this as a short checklist and update threads with status.

Action items:
1) Rishi: provision the dedicated staging endpoint and generate the short-lived token (TEST-FINWISE-20270420). Confirm expiry and rotation plan.
2) Dev: prepare a stub k6 script that exercises both generation and streaming flows (we can start with their scripts but have a Redwood version to validate load shapes). Attach sample scenarios: 
   - 70% standard generation (prompt -> full response)
   - 30% streaming chat (measure first-chunk latency)
3) Rishi/Dev: provide the IP ranges to FinWise for allowlisting and confirm if any additional firewall/NAT entries required.
4) Logan: coordinate with FinWise on exact run times and get their k6 scripts repo link.
5) Marissa: I'll prepare a short runbook PDF and a post-run data collection template for SLO evaluation.

Please update with ETA for each item. We should plan a 30-minute dry-run the morning of Apr 20 to validate connectivity and tokens.

- Staging endpoint: https://staging-api.redwood.example/finwise
- API token: TEST-FINWISE-20270420 (expires 2027-04-22T00:00:00Z)

- Notes:

  - Please avoid long-running single-session chats that keep connections open for hours; that can artificially lower concurrency headroom.

Attachments (zipped into this thread):
- load-test-runbook.pdf (runbook and measurement checklist)
- k6_script_v1.js (Redwood k6 stub that hits generation and streaming endpoints)
- test-credentials.txt (token and endpoint summary)
